Hi Irene,

Thanks again for taking our call last week. As we scope our pilots we need to complete the TIA questionnaire and confirm how Redwood's subprocessors and routing policies interact with the UK IDTA/UK Addendum expectations. We have three priority asks: 

1) Confirm whether Redwood will accept a UK Addendum with the standard conditional language we use for UK personal data.
2) Provide a current subprocessor map (name, role, country, data access level) and whether any subprocessors can be contractually restricted from routing into the US.
3) Clarify technical safeguards for data at rest when transferred to third parties (KMS approach, HSM, key separation).

I've attached our TIA questionnaire to this message (CareHealth_TIA_questionnaire.xlsx). For now please treat the timeline as tight—procurement would like evidence and DPA redlines within 10 business days.

Appreciate a quick confirmation of the two items above and any heads-up on likely exceptions.

Thanks,

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the note and the attached spreadsheet. We're happy to work through this quickly. A few upfront signals to set expectations: 

- UK Addendum: Redwood accepts the UK Addendum in principle. We do have a small set of conditional items we flag for enterprise accounts (routing exceptions for production disaster recovery, certain analytics subprocessors that require US infra). We'll call these out explicitly in the DPA redline so procurement can triage.

- Subprocessor map: attaching the current export (redwood_subprocessor_map_v3.csv). High level: most infra subprocessors operate in EU or US; a handful of managed tooling vendors have cross-border support. We can mark which subprocessors are eligible for routing restrictions and which are not (some are multi-region SaaS services).

- KMS/key separation: Redwood uses customer-scoped KMS integration for Private deployments (customers can bring keys). For Hosted and Dedicated we use tenant-specific key material and an HSM-backed envelope encryption scheme. We do not currently offer per-customer HSMs on hosted tiers; that would be a contractual enterprise option.

Action items for our side: 
- Legal to prepare a DPA redline that accepts UK Addendum with a short exceptions section.
- Security to populate the TIA answers for technical controls and provide anonymized logs and export controls.
- Ops to mark subprocessors that can be restricted by routing policy.

Marissa / Priyom — looping you in for legal redlines and subprocessor gating. Sanjay — can you confirm whether CareHealth requires all subprocessors to be UK/EU-only or just an enforceable routing restriction for certain data classes? That will change our proposal.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Privacy & Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

Hi Irene / Marissa,

Thanks for the quick reply and the subprocessor map. To clarify our position: CareHealth's procurement will accept a routing restriction as long as the DPA includes an enforceable routing policy (i.e., Redwood must ensure requests are pinned to EU/UK-only subprocessors for the specified processing activities and log any automatic fallback to other regions). For a limited set of analytics subprocessors we can accept pseudonymized exports to the US provided additional safeguards (contractual anonymity guarantees; no patient identifiers).

On KMS: procurement prefers customer-managed keys where possible but understands it is a higher tier. Please confirm if the DPA can include a commitment to offer KMIP/HSM integration for private/on-prem and an evaluation timeline for extending that to Dedicated customers.

We also need evidence (redacted) of key rotation policies and details on cryptographic modules in use. Can Redwood supply an HSM attestation or a SOC 2 control description?

Thanks,
Legal Ops (CareHealth NHS)
